bridges.statement: The cumulative evidence warrants belief that God exists.
The universe's existence, intelligibility, power, beauty, and fine-tuning point to a transcendent rational source.
Objective morality, dignity, justice, and accountability are better grounded in God than in materialism.
God's historical self-revelation in Jesus, especially the resurrection, supports Christian theism.
Mind, meaning, information, and rationality resist reduction to matter and fit a rational divine source.
The cross and promised justice provide grounds for trust and hope amid suffering.
Divine agency and scientific mechanisms are compatible explanatory levels.

routes.speaker: Michael Shermer
routes.position: Evidence does not warrant belief in God.

bridges.statement: The presented evidence does not warrant belief in God.
Belief should be proportioned to testable evidence, with uncertainty preferred to unsupported supernatural conclusions.
Naturalistic inquiry offers investigable explanations and exposes supernatural language as explanatorily empty.
Evolution and sociality can explain moral capacities without God.
Unanswered suffering and failed prayer count against the loving interventionist God presented.
Mental functions and consciousness emerge from, and depend upon, physical brains.
Religious belief varies culturally, so prevalence, comfort, and testimony do not establish truth.

sections.title: Cosmic origins, intelligibility, fine-tuning, and regress
Morality, evolution, justice, and human dignity
Historical Christianity, resurrection, revelation, and diversity
Science, agency, worldview comparison, and closing positions

moves.speaker: Michael Shermer
quoteEligibleExactSpans: we usually back into those beliefs after the fact
determined by where we happen to have been born
moves.proposition: People often commit to beliefs first and later construct reasons for them, while birthplace, parents, culture, and peers largely shape those beliefs.
moves.inventoryRationale: Establishes Shermer's account of belief formation and cultural dependence.

moves.speaker: Michael Shermer
quoteEligibleExactSpans: they're socially constructed they were part of the culture
it's okay to go one God farther
moves.proposition: Because discarded gods such as Zeus and Thor lack evidence and were socially constructed, Shermer extends the same skepticism one god further.
moves.inventoryRationale: Applies religious diversity and cultural construction directly to the motion.

moves.speaker: Michael Shermer
quoteEligibleExactSpans: atheism is just a lack of belief in a god
it isn't a position to take
moves.proposition: Atheism here is simply a lack of belief in God, not a political-style platform, religion, or affirmative doctrine.
moves.inventoryRationale: Defines Shermer's calibrated burden and prevents misattributing strong atheism to him.

moves.speaker: Michael Shermer
quoteEligibleExactSpans: why can't it be a nonentity
that gets us into an infinite regress
moves.proposition: A cause of the universe need not be an entity; requiring a creator of any universe merely produces an unhelpful infinite regress.
moves.inventoryRationale: States Shermer's central objection to cosmological inference.

moves.speaker: Michael Shermer
quoteEligibleExactSpans: our brains are too restricted to limited in our capacity
supernatural it's just a word
moves.proposition: Human cognitive limits counsel humility, while calling an unsolved mystery supernatural merely substitutes a label for an explanation.
moves.inventoryRationale: Defines the explanatory standard behind Shermer's rejection of God-of-the-gaps reasoning.

moves.speaker: Michael Shermer
quoteEligibleExactSpans: it is pretty amazing how all the laws of nature are configured
humility modesty in the face of the great unknown is proper
moves.proposition: Fine-tuning is striking, but four centuries of science do not justify declaring natural explanation impossible and inferring a supernatural force.
moves.inventoryRationale: Concedes the phenomenon while rejecting the proposed inference.

moves.speaker: Michael Shermer
quoteEligibleExactSpans: there might be multiple universes
try to answer it scientifically
moves.proposition: Multiple universes, including speculative black-hole-generated universes, illustrate testable natural research programs that should be explored before design is inferred.
moves.inventoryRationale: Supplies Shermer's naturalistic alternative to a design conclusion.

moves.speaker: Michael Shermer
quoteEligibleExactSpans: we're a social primate species
a propensity to be pro-social and cooperative
moves.proposition: Morality arose among social primates through pressures favoring cooperation within groups, alongside evolved competition and distrust between groups.
moves.inventoryRationale: Presents the main evolutionary account of moral behavior.

moves.speaker: Michael Shermer
quoteEligibleExactSpans: a scientists have nothing to say about it because we study natural law
pray for people don't do any better
moves.proposition: Testable studies asking whether people recover faster when prayed for have found no improvement over people not prayed for.
moves.inventoryRationale: Combines the demarcation issue with Shermer's principal empirical prayer objection.

moves.speaker: Michael Shermer
quoteEligibleExactSpans: it's not a frivolous argument
not one of them has grown a new limb
miracles always happen to be things that might have happened anyway
moves.proposition: No prayed-for amputee has regrown a limb, whereas attributed healings involve outcomes such as tumor remission that can occur naturally.
moves.inventoryRationale: Sharpens the evidential and moral challenge to selective miracle attribution.

moves.speaker: Michael Shermer
quoteEligibleExactSpans: if you know the technology then it isn't God
you'll never find a dieta
I don't see that there's any reason to believe in God
moves.proposition: Reasoning from extraordinary powers can establish at most an advanced intelligent being, not a deity, so the evidence presented gives no reason for God-belief.
moves.inventoryRationale: States Shermer's opening bottom line and limits what apparent agency could establish.

moves.speaker: John Lennox
quoteEligibleExactSpans: reason and faith are opposed
the evidence for God's existence does not start with pure reason
God's self-revelation to which human reason can respond
moves.proposition: Rational belief need not rest on proof by pure reason; alleged divine self-revelation may instead be critically tested for coherence and correspondence with reality.
moves.inventoryRationale: Sets Lennox's epistemology and cumulative evidential method.

moves.speaker: John Lennox
quoteEligibleExactSpans: this universe cannot be all that exists
it points beyond itself to a source
the universe is not self explanatory

responseComponents.component: The universe is not self-explanatory, so explanation beyond it remains legitimate rather than automatically regressive.
The inference is presented as a positive response to cosmic power and intelligibility, not merely a label for ignorance.

moves.proposition: The universe's non-self-explanatory character points beyond itself toward a nonphysical source of intelligence and power.
moves.inventoryRationale: States Lennox's main cosmological inference and directly counters the non-answer objection.

moves.speaker: John Lennox
quoteEligibleExactSpans: science has done nothing to diminish that impression
the biblical doctrine of creation
the methodology of modern science
moves.proposition: Science has not displaced a creator; Lennox cites the biblical doctrine of creation as a historical source of modern scientific methodology.
moves.inventoryRationale: Introduces Lennox's compatibility and historical-origin case.

moves.speaker: John Lennox
quoteEligibleExactSpans: the almost unbelievable complexity of the arrangements
the impression of design
concluding from its advances that it's pointing towards the existence of God

responseComponents.component: Scientific advances revealing complexity and fine-tuning can positively strengthen a design inference rather than merely expose ignorance.
Speculative natural alternatives do not erase the observed impression of intelligence in life and physical law.

moves.proposition: DNA's complexity and cosmic fine-tuning are presented as positive indications of intelligence and design, not merely placeholders for missing science.
moves.inventoryRationale: Develops the design strand of Lennox's cumulative route.

moves.speaker: John Lennox
quoteEligibleExactSpans: morality is neither subjective Nora lative
atheists can be good
atheism does not explain

responseComponents.component: Evolutionary behavior may explain why people act morally, but not why some acts are objectively and absolutely wrong.

moves.proposition: Atheists can be moral and religious people immoral, but Lennox argues that atheism does not explain judgments that some acts are absolutely wrong.
moves.inventoryRationale: Preserves Lennox's explicit concession while distinguishing moral behavior from moral ontology.

moves.speaker: John Lennox
quoteEligibleExactSpans: if there is no final accountability after death
will ever see justice done
justice will be done by God
moves.proposition: Without final accountability after death, mass murderers can escape permanently and their victims will never see justice done.
moves.inventoryRationale: Adds final accountability and hope to the moral case.

moves.speaker: John Lennox
quoteEligibleExactSpans: you're absolutely right
revealed himself in history and experience
the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead

responseComponents.component: Lennox concedes creation and conscience yield at most generic theism, then introduces historical evidence to identify the Christian God.

moves.proposition: Creation and conscience cannot establish Christianity specifically; Lennox therefore appeals to alleged revelation in Jesus and historical evidence concerning his resurrection.
moves.inventoryRationale: Important concession and transition from generic theism to Christian theism.

moves.speaker: John Lennox
quoteEligibleExactSpans: happened by a colossal input of divine power
if all that exists is nature
our conviction can be trusted
moves.proposition: If rational convictions are merely products of an irrational natural process, strict naturalism gives no ground for trusting that they track external reality.
moves.inventoryRationale: Links miracle possibility to Lennox's argument from reason.

moves.speaker: John Lennox
quoteEligibleExactSpans: the disciples must have seen something
historically and psychologically absurd
the birth and rapid rise of the Christian Church
moves.proposition: The disciples' apparent lack of conscious deception and the church's rapid rise require explanation, for which resurrection is offered as the church's own account.
moves.inventoryRationale: Records the specific historical inference supporting resurrection.

moves.speaker: John Lennox
quoteEligibleExactSpans: I'm ashamed as a Christian of what has been done in Christ's name
this is the hardest question of all
God has not remained distant from the problem of human suffering

responseComponents.component: Lennox concedes suffering is the hardest problem and rejects simplistic answers, but argues the crucified God participates in suffering.

moves.proposition: Suffering is the hardest objection and admits no simplistic answer, yet the cross portrays God entering human suffering rather than remaining distant.
moves.inventoryRationale: Preserves Lennox's concession and principal Christian response to evil.

moves.speaker: John Lennox
quoteEligibleExactSpans: historical evidence that Jesus Christ had not risen from the dead
my faith is based on evidence
evidence is crucial for me
moves.attributionBasis: The host's question is excluded; Lennox's answer begins at event 973.
moves.proposition: Historical evidence that Jesus did not rise from the dead could cause Lennox to abandon belief in God.
moves.inventoryRationale: Important statement of falsifiability and evidential commitment.

moves.speaker: Michael Shermer
quoteEligibleExactSpans: mind is a word to describe behaviors
a bottom-up process
consciousness is an emergent property
moves.attributionBasis: Clear Shermer answer after the audience question has ended.
moves.proposition: Specific thoughts and behaviors can be investigated neuroscientifically, and consciousness is understood as an emergent property of patterned neural activity.
moves.inventoryRationale: States Shermer's materialist account of mind.

moves.speaker: John Lennox
quoteEligibleExactSpans: there's not a scrap of evidence for it
no one knows what consciousness is
information is not a material quantity

responseComponents.component: Neural emergence is asserted beyond the evidence because consciousness remains unexplained and information is not itself a material quantity.

moves.proposition: Reducing consciousness to neural firing outruns present evidence, while reductionism cannot explain immaterial information.
moves.inventoryRationale: Major direct rebuttal to Shermer's emergent materialism.

moves.speaker: John Lennox
quoteEligibleExactSpans: in terms of the physics and chemistry of the paper and ink it cannot be done
something that carries meaning
the first one undermines rationality
moves.proposition: The physics and chemistry of paper and ink do not explain a menu's semantic content; Lennox therefore argues that meaning requires intelligence.
moves.inventoryRationale: Provides Lennox's menu-and-meaning illustration and worldview comparison.

moves.speaker: Michael Shermer
quoteEligibleExactSpans: if you have a stroke in the Broca's area
if the neurons are dead that's it
it's nothing more than neurons
moves.attributionBasis: Clear Shermer interjection replying to Lennox.

responseComponents.component: Localized brain damage abolishing language is offered as evidence that mental capacities depend on neurons.
The loss of higher-order language when neural tissue dies challenges its proposed independence from matter.

moves.proposition: Damage to language-specific brain regions eliminates language, evidencing that higher mental functions depend on neural tissue.
moves.inventoryRationale: Shermer's strongest direct neuroscience reply.

moves.speaker: John Lennox
quoteEligibleExactSpans: if you damage my brain that will cease to exist
that is not an argument to say the two things are the same thing
the meaning of the writing
moves.attributionBasis: Clear Lennox response after brief moderation.

responseComponents.component: Dependence of information on a physical carrier does not establish identity between meaning and its material medium.

moves.proposition: Brain dependence does not prove mind-brain identity, just as destruction of paper destroys writing without making meaning identical to ink.
moves.inventoryRationale: Directly distinguishes dependence from ontological identity.

moves.speaker: Michael Shermer
quoteEligibleExactSpans: the God that john believes in however we have a problem
why innocent children should die
god works in mysterious ways answered that's not an answer
moves.attributionBasis: Clear Shermer answer after the host's framing ends.

responseComponents.component: Divine participation in suffering does not explain why a loving God permits innocent children to die or selectively withholds healing.

moves.proposition: An evil god remains possible, but Lennox's loving God leaves innocent suffering and selective non-healing unexplained.
moves.inventoryRationale: Clarifies that the evidential problem targets Lennox's specific conception of God.

moves.speaker: John Lennox
quoteEligibleExactSpans: this is the hardest problem
this is a damaged world
enough evidence to trust him even when there are major problems

responseComponents.component: Lennox concedes the damaged world's suffering lacks a complete explanation but argues the cross supplies sufficient grounds for trust amid unresolved problems.

moves.proposition: Amid a damaged world, God's alleged participation in human suffering through Christ gives Lennox grounds to trust God despite unresolved problems.
moves.inventoryRationale: Most developed direct response to the problem of natural evil.

moves.speaker: Michael Shermer
quoteEligibleExactSpans: those beliefs saved me
irrelevant about whether the beliefs claimed by Scientology are true
quite a separate question from whether there really is a god
moves.attributionBasis: Clear Shermer answer following Lennox's testimony.

responseComponents.component: A belief's power to comfort sufferers does not show that its supernatural claims are true.
Scientology provides comparable resilience, illustrating that psychological benefit cannot adjudicate competing religions.

moves.proposition: Religious beliefs may comfort and rebuild a life, but those psychological benefits do not establish that the beliefs are true.
moves.inventoryRationale: Important concession coupled with a direct rebuttal to experiential and hope-based evidence.

moves.speaker: John Lennox
quoteEligibleExactSpans: it doesn't determine truth
the same argument applies to atheism
we've got to break out of that

responseComponents.component: Lennox agrees comfort does not determine truth but says psychological explanations likewise cannot establish atheism; evidence must decide.

moves.proposition: Comfort does not determine truth, and that point applies equally to religion and atheism, so the dispute must return to evidence.
moves.inventoryRationale: Preserves an explicit agreement and Lennox's symmetrical qualification.

moves.speaker: Michael Shermer
quoteEligibleExactSpans: there's a lot of scientists that aren't baffled by it
irrelevant how many people believe something
these things are either real or they're not
moves.attributionBasis: Clear Shermer response during debate exchange.

responseComponents.component: Quoting prominent converts or scientists impressed by DNA does not establish design when other experts disagree.
The number of resurrection believers is irrelevant to whether the event occurred.
Historical influence and popularity must be separated from the truth of the resurrection explanation.

moves.proposition: Expert authority and numbers of believers are irrelevant to whether design or resurrection claims are real.
moves.inventoryRationale: Consolidates Shermer's direct evidential critique of Lennox's appeals to testimony and prevalence.

moves.speaker: Michael Shermer
quoteEligibleExactSpans: this business of the selfish genes
being extremely cooperative pro-social altruistic
having a moral sense
moves.attributionBasis: Clear Shermer answer in the moral exchange.

responseComponents.component: Gene-level evolution does not entail selfish behavior; in social mammals it favors cooperation, altruism, and moral sentiments.
An evolved moral sense can motivate justice-seeking in this life without postmortem accountability.

moves.proposition: Evolutionary success means transmitting genes, and among social mammals cooperation, altruism, and an in-group moral sense can promote that success.
moves.inventoryRationale: Directly answers Lennox's claim that evolutionary materialism cannot yield moral agency.

moves.speaker: John Lennox
quoteEligibleExactSpans: people of all kinds of different backgrounds
exactly what you would expect if Christianity were true
falls down a bit when it comes to genuine altruism

responseComponents.component: Cross-cultural moral commonality also fits humans bearing God's image, while Lennox argues evolutionary accounts struggle with altruism toward unrelated outsiders.

moves.proposition: Similar moral intuitions across backgrounds are what Christianity predicts if all people are created in God's image as moral beings.
moves.inventoryRationale: Records Lennox's direct reinterpretation and residual explanatory challenge.

moves.speaker: Michael Shermer
quoteEligibleExactSpans: some Christians who got behind it
it isn't like Christianity was behind this the whole way
shifted toward more and more inclusiveness
moves.attributionBasis: Clear Shermer response to Lennox's historical claim.

responseComponents.component: Christian abolitionists faced prolonged Christian resistance, so abolition cannot simply be credited to Christianity as a whole.

moves.proposition: Christian abolitionists had to overcome substantial Christian resistance, so Christianity as a whole was not consistently behind abolition.
moves.inventoryRationale: Important rebuttal concerning Christianity's claimed historical moral fruits.

moves.speaker: John Lennox
quoteEligibleExactSpans: Christians equally convinced of the reliability and inspiration of Scripture who differ
a universe that's around 15 billion years old
moves.attributionBasis: Clear Lennox answer after audience question.
moves.proposition: Commitment to scriptural authority does not require young-earth creationism; Lennox accepts the scientific evidence for an ancient universe.
moves.inventoryRationale: Important concession showing his theism is compatible with mainstream cosmic chronology.

moves.speaker: John Lennox
quoteEligibleExactSpans: there are Nobel laureates on both sides
it's not science abolishing God
the world views are opposed
moves.attributionBasis: Clear Lennox response to Shermer's scientist statistics.

responseComponents.component: Lennox accepts that headcounts do not prove God, but disagreement among leading scientists shows science itself does not settle the worldview question.

moves.proposition: The presence of Nobel laureates on both sides shows that the conflict is between naturalism and theism, not science and religion.
moves.inventoryRationale: Major worldview-level concession and reply about scientific authority.

moves.speaker: John Lennox
quoteEligibleExactSpans: I believe in the God who groans the whole endeavor of science
confusing agency with mechanism
I see God not in the bits of the universe I don't understand

responseComponents.component: God is proposed as the agency grounding the whole lawful system, not as a placeholder for gaps in its mechanisms.

moves.proposition: Divine agency and scientific mechanism are compatible; discovering a mechanism need not remove God as the agent responsible for the whole system.
moves.inventoryRationale: Lennox's principal closing rebuttal to the God-of-the-gaps charge.

moves.speaker: John Lennox
quoteEligibleExactSpans: if he insists on asking who created god
none of us believes in a created God
the buck will stop somewhere on both sides

responseComponents.component: Both worldviews terminate explanation somewhere; theism terminates in an uncreated God, while naturalism terminates in matter and energy.

moves.proposition: Asking who created God misconstrues classical theism because it assumes a created God; every worldview must ultimately stop at something uncreated.
moves.inventoryRationale: Direct closing answer to Shermer's regress objection.

moves.speaker: John Lennox
quoteEligibleExactSpans: it would be wise to check it all out
belief in God is in the end commitment to a person
on the basis of the evidence you've accumulated
moves.proposition: Cumulative evidence from science, history, philosophy, and alleged divine revelation can provide a rational platform for personal commitment to God.
moves.inventoryRationale: States Lennox's final cumulative epistemic position without reducing it to one argument.

moves.speaker: Michael Shermer
quoteEligibleExactSpans: militant agnostic I don't know and you don't either
none of us know
it's okay in science to just say I don't know

responseComponents.component: Shermer argues that unresolved questions about origins, evil, and suffering warrant continued inquiry and admitted ignorance rather than commitment.

moves.proposition: On questions such as suffering and pre-Big-Bang origins, neither speaker knows; science properly admits uncertainty while continuing investigation.
moves.inventoryRationale: Captures Shermer's calibrated closing epistemology.

selectionRationale: The forty-one chronological moves remain distinct and load-bearing after removing con-16, which duplicated con-03's definition of atheism. The three-move total difference reflects source structure rather than manufactured symmetry. Belief-and-evidence retains four Lennox moves and three Shermer moves covering distinct evidential burdens; science-agency-and-worldviews retains four Lennox moves because his historical compatibility claim, scientists-on-both-sides inference, agency-mechanism reply, and uncreated-terminus argument are independently assessable, while Shermer's closing uncertainty argument is the section's single distinct con move. Every other section contains two to four moves per side, and no move was added, merged, or reassigned after judgment because no judgment exists yet.
